title: Pensioner benefits
headline: £187.5bn by 2029-30. Outside the welfare cap.
description: Change spending on the state pension and other pensioner benefits from April 2027, as a percentage of the OBR's forecast (£187.5bn in 2029-30). A 1% change is about £1.9bn a year. This line sits outside the welfare cap.

baselinePolicy.text: Pensioner spending, which the OBR defines as state pension, pension credit, pensioner housing benefit and winter fuel payments, of £161.2bn in 2025-26 rising to £187.5bn in 2029-30 and £196.2bn in 2030-31 (Table 4.6).
alreadyIncludes: Triple-lock uprating of the state pension and larger cohorts reaching state pension age, adding 0.6% of GDP to pensioner spending by 2030-31 (EFO paragraph 4.23).
The rise in the state pension age from 66 to 67 between 2026 and 2028, reducing pensioner spending by roughly 0.3% of GDP in 2030-31 (EFO paragraph 4.23).
Winter fuel payments for pensioners with taxable income of £35,000 or less from winter 2025 (Budget 2025, Table 4.1 line 84).

control.formatLabel: of forecast spending on this line

caveats: Welfare-cap treatment is approximated by line: this whole line is counted outside the cap because the state pension dominates it. Pension credit, pensioner housing benefit and winter fuel payments are in fact inside the cap.
A uniform percentage change to a forecast line is a stylised device standing in for the many policies that could deliver it (rates, uprating, eligibility); no behavioural response is included.

considerations.text: The OBR attributes the rise in pensioner spending to larger state pension cohorts (about 850,000 people reaching state pension age a year by 2030-31, up from 700,000 in 2022-23) and triple-lock uprating, partly offset by the higher state pension age. Changing this line in practice means changing uprating or eligibility rules whose costs depend on earnings and inflation.

interactions.text: Winter fuel payments are part of pensioner spending, so the two changes overlap.
